evidence.quote: Valar Atomics announced a partnership with Nvidia to explore AI data centers powered directly by advanced nuclear energy, marking a first for the industry.
evidence.one_line: Valar Atomics announced a partnership with Nvidia to explore AI data centers powered by advanced nuclear energy (on 2026-07-01 announcement).
evidence.speaker: Valar Atomics

evidence.quote: The companies are considering a 30-megawatt, nearly waterless data center in Utah using Valar’s Ward250 reactor and Nvidia’s water-efficient cooling technology.
evidence.one_line: The companies are considering a 30 MW, nearly waterless data center in Utah using the Ward250 reactor and Nvidia cooling technology.
evidence.speaker: Valar Atomics and Nvidia

evidence.quote: Valar Atomics and Nvidia are exploring the deployment of a 30 megawatt data center, fully powered by their nuclear reactor.
evidence.one_line: Valar and Nvidia are exploring a 30 MW data center fully powered by the Ward250 reactor.
evidence.speaker: Valar Atomics and Nvidia

evidence.quote: Their reactor, the Ward250, went critical on June 18, and it is now generating 100 kilowatts of electricity.
evidence.one_line: Ward250 reactor went critical on June 18 and is generating 100 kW of electricity.
evidence.speaker: Valar Atomics

evidence.quote: Before Valar Atomics can generate power commercially, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission will need to license their reactor. In a recent editorial board meeting with the Deseret News, NRC chairman Ho Nieh said the commission is hoping to shorten federal licensing review times to less than 18 months.
evidence.one_line: NRC chairman Ho Nieh said the commission hopes to shorten federal licensing review times to less than 18 months.
evidence.speaker: Ho Nieh

evidence.quote: The proposed size is 300 times smaller than the approved Stratos data center in Box Elder County.
evidence.one_line: The proposed 30 MW data center is 300 times smaller than the approved Stratos data center in Box Elder County.
evidence.speaker: Deseret News
